entries.summary: The new optional findings field distinguishes an empty array (explicit plan-wide objection) from an absent field (verdict predates the contract), which is what lets the contested-bead consumer migrate off prose scanning without changing behaviour.

entries.title: sandbox-deploy read-only token tests must force the real fleet.key absent
entries.summary: tryLoadToken() in scripts/sandbox-deploy.mjs never overrides home, so a no-mint assertion is vacuous on any machine with a real ~/.apra-fleet/fleet.key unless that one read is mocked to ENOENT.

entries.title: Setup shell's $$ is unsafe to record for liveness checks under Git Bash on Windows
entries.summary: scripts/sandbox-lock.mjs's acquire CLI previously recorded the Setup shell's self-reported $$, which under Git Bash on Windows is an MSYS-internal pid invisible to defaultDeps.isAlive's native process.kill(pid,0) check -- fixed by having the CLI record its own process.ppid instead, since the CLI process is itself a direct child of the Setup shell and process.ppid always resolves in the native OS pid namespace.

entries.title: A supervisor test built without token/dataDir silently disables auth and passes vacuously
entries.summary: createSupervisor leaves token null when neither deps.token nor deps.dataDir is given, and the per-request guard is conditioned on that token, so guarded-route tests on such a supervisor prove nothing about auth.

entries.title: Reaping a reservation must return the post-write agent, and refusals must run before it
entries.summary: reapIfDead() writes through updateAgent, so callers reading the pre-reap Agent object still see the cleared holder; and any refusal branch placed after reaping makes a 'refused, wrote nothing' call mutate the member.

entries.title: bd-replay record mode bypasses the real-mode caches, so recordings are 1:1 with issued calls
entries.summary: runCmd applies the dolt-sync/sync.remote/read caches only when bdMode() === 'real'; record mode sends every bd call other than dolt-sync and the synthesized ones (bd where, bd memories --json, bd forget) to recordBd, and recordBd rewrites the whole fixture with writeFileSync rather than appending.

entries.title: apra-fleet start's already-running reuse path exits before rewriting server.json
entries.summary: src/index.ts exits 0 on a live instance before createHttpTransport and the server.json write, so a no-op start never refreshes server.json; the recorded port is the only way to detect a wrong-port instance.

entries.title: After a handled terminating signal, run-all-tests.mjs deferred hard-kill timer must own the exit
entries.summary: The group SIGTERM reaps the shell:true wrapper quickly, so the suite loop would fall through to the trailing process.exit before the deferred killTree; deferredExitPending gates that exit and the timer kills the pgid captured at signal time.

entries.title: runSprintCycle now hosts zero inline phase bodies, and that is mechanically pinned rather than described
entries.summary: After the final slice, runner.js builds no phase() label at all; phase-sequence-order.test.mjs asserts a zero-match shape scan over runner.js with a >=12 count across phases/* as its non-vacuity control.

entries.title: resolveFleetServerConnection falls back to stdio instead of throwing when no HTTP singleton is running
entries.summary: The client resolver throws for an unreachable server only when APRA_FLEET_TRANSPORT=http is set; by default it returns a stdio self-spawn resolution, so "server not started yet" is not an exception path.

entries.title: explicit-id-create guard now uses a call-expression-agnostic command-literal rule, unioned with the command() site rule
entries.summary: The guard no longer depends on findCallSites recognising the enclosing call identifier. A second rule flags any string literal whose content begins with the bd create command and continues into an argument, so wrappers, renamed bindings and method calls are covered.

entries.title: Supervisor project folder is a JSON bootstrap file, not a project-store row, because it resolves before any store opens
entries.summary: supervisor.config.json (owned solely by project-config.mjs) is a separate, simpler state layer from the node:sqlite project store -- it must resolve at the top of serve.mjs startup, before the sqlite store (Node 22.13.0+, can fail to open) is known to be available.

entries.title: Streak id survives on the beads even though the lane grouping drops it from its return contract
entries.summary: groupStreaksFromLaneMetadata discards the lane id from its return value, but every bead in the returned arrays still carries metadata.streak, so streak identity is recoverable per-bead on that one path.

entries.title: provisionOutcome's prose fallback in vcs-auth.mjs is live and deliberately pinned
entries.summary: An earlier KB entry calling that fallback dead code and constant-true is wrong: the [FAIL] prose regex still fires even though wrapTool never sets isError, and two tests pin the behaviour.

entries.title: The generic-boundary scanner narrows fleet-sprint/skills markdown to the bead-id rule only
entries.summary: ENGINE_FILE_SET lists fleet-sprint/skills/**.md with ids restricted to ['bead-id-in-llm-text'], so apra-fleet-specific content (its binary name, localhost:8787, packages/apra-fleet-se paths) is legitimate there -- but a bead id still fails the build.

entries.title: ServiceManager.stop is a graceful HTTP shutdown with its own 5s window, then a SIGTERM that re-arms launchd KeepAlive
entries.summary: On macOS and Linux, ServiceManager.stop delegates to gracefulStopByServerJson (POST shutdown, 5s poll, SIGTERM fallback) and never unloads the job; a SIGTERM fallback can trigger a supervisor relaunch.

entries.title: Local vs remote member dispatch paths
entries.summary: Local members share the orchestrator's own machine and credentials, so no SSH or file probe is needed -- check agent.agentType === 'local' and short-circuit. Remote members require actual SSH connectivity and credential probes.

entries.title: Verify a move-only runner.js extraction by normalized line-set diff plus a runtime export-surface diff
entries.summary: Two mechanical checks prove a fleet-sprint move-only extraction without reading the moved code: set-compare the removed lines against the new module after normalizing comment prefixes and the export keyword, then import the old and new runner.js side by side and diff Object.keys.

entries.title: Structured tool response shapes are pinned to the client typedefs by a ROOT vitest test
entries.summary: tests/structured-tool-responses.test.ts check 4 diffs four server *Fields interfaces against api.mjs typedefs both ways, so a new structuredContent field without the client typedef turns root npm test red.

entries.title: ctx.policies is the seam that makes 'this variance is a policy field, not an engine branch' falsifiable
entries.summary: dispatchRole reads its row through ctx.policies when supplied, so a test can splice ONE field of ONE row and observe the engine behave differently; without it the claim that a variance is data rather than a branch cannot be tested at all.

entries.title: Not every bd list --parent read in fleet-sprint needs closed children -- only computeChildFloor does
entries.summary: computeChildFloor must count CLOSED children (id-floor / re-mint prevention) so it passes --all, while phases/plan.mjs pending-rejected-newTask reconciliation and parent-notes-staleness.mjs deliberately read only default (open) children.

entries.title: role-policies.mjs's secondary() dispatch inherits its main dispatch's member field unless explicitly overridden
entries.summary: secondary(main, role, kind, over) spreads ...main first, so a role's resume/re-ask dispatch shares the SAME member object as its main dispatch for every role in the table today -- any consumer matching dispatches by member-routing expression must de-duplicate across [entry, entry.secondary] or it double-counts one real call site.

entries.title: A source-level watchdog explicitness check must resolve secondary-declared roles to their base row
entries.summary: ROLE_NAMES includes doer-resume, which is declared via secondary(doer, 'doer-resume', ...) and has no policy('doer-resume', ...) literal, so a per-role source scan for an explicit watchdog declaration fails unless it follows the secondary back to its base.

entries.title: shell-ui typecheck requires apra-fleet-ui-kit to be built first
entries.summary: packages/apra-fleet-shell-ui consumes the ui-kit through a file: dependency whose types point at ./dist, so any build wiring must compile apra-fleet-ui-kit before typechecking or building the shell.

entries.title: Three distinct git-credential-helper file shapes exist across member OS/shell combinations
entries.summary: The deployed credential helper differs by member OS AND shell: POSIX (linux/macos) writes an extensionless $HOME script, windows-powershell writes $env:USERPROFILE\...bat, and windows-gitbash writes a .bat under $HOME but is invoked through bash -- so any read-side builder needs all three forms plus the PowerShell call operator.

entries.title: loadOrCreateToken torn-write recovery has a knowingly accepted divergence window
entries.summary: The supervisor token mint deliberately keeps one race open -- a blank token file plus a peer mid-wx-write -- because closing it with write-temp-then-rename would forfeit atomic create-with-mode-0600.

entries.title: A directly launched sprint's deployer self-id is the branch name, not a ledger uuid
entries.summary: runner.js derives the deployer's own reservation id as validated.runId || validated.branch, so a standalone (non-supervisor) launch hands the deployer a branch name rather than a supervisor sprintId.

entries.title: bin/serve.mjs opens one projects-store handle and shares it across every route module
entries.summary: registerOwnerRefsRoute and registerProjectRoutes both take the openStore()-shaped {db, path, version, applied, close} handle as their 'store' dependency, not the raw db, and serve.mjs opens exactly one such handle for all of them.

entries.title: Mocked-fetch UI tests cannot catch a console-route zod contract mismatch
entries.summary: A shell-ui action button that posts only member_id passes its mocked-fetch test but 400s at runtime for every /api/fleet/ tool whose zod schema has a required non-member field.

entries.title: Neither supervisor-harness export serves a test needing a real listener plus post-construction routes
entries.summary: startTestSupervisor returns no supervisor handle so routes cannot be registered after it starts, and createTestSupervisor returns a handle but never starts a listener -- a test needing both must build its own supervisor.

entries.title: Falsify a fleet-sprint or root-repo test without ever mutating the tracked tree
entries.summary: Copy the module directory to /tmp and revert the single file there, or reconstruct a pure function in a standalone script -- mutating tracked source in place risks a torn read under the concurrent suites and can leave the file corrupted.

entries.title: memberHeldCheck is the single combined member-held gate for member_owner and remove_member
entries.summary: One exported helper merges the sync reservedBy check with the async workflow-package holds consult, with a deliberately asymmetric fail-closed rule keyed on the owning package(s).

entries.title: bd show on a missing id exits 1, so every fleet-sprint existence probe lands in its catch branch
entries.summary: bd show <missing-id> --json exits 1 with an error envelope rather than returning [], and FleetWorkflow.command() throws on any non-zero exit, so an existence probe's catch branch is the NORMAL path, not the rare one.

entries.title: The mock-sprint and golden suites leak temp files, so 'no artifacts outside the sandbox' cannot be shown by running them
entries.summary: One full mock-sprint pass leaves exactly 10 fleet-sprint-body-*.txt files in the system temp dir and the golden 3-bead suite leaves one sprint-lock entry, independently of any gate that spawns them; npm test already does this twice today.

entries.title: compose_permissions reports a refusal as text, not a thrown error, so the fleet-sprint provisioner must judge success from call status
entries.summary: The pre-dispatch runbook-permissions provisioner cannot rely on a try/catch to detect a denied grant, because compose_permissions returns a refusal (e.g. its never-auto-grant denylist) as a normal text response rather than throwing.

entries.title: Supervisor shutdownRequested resolves only after full teardown
entries.summary: server.mjs stop() is idempotent and calls shutdownResolve() last, after server.close() and every seam stop, so code after `await supervisor.shutdownRequested` in bin/serve.mjs runs strictly last for both the signal and the /api/shutdown paths.

entries.title: Project-scope kb_export is additive and basis-filtered; global scope still rewrites
entries.summary: kb_export scope=project never removes or rewrites existing bible entries and adds only CONFIRMED entries whose source_file_hashes basis matches the files on disk; with nothing to add it leaves the file untouched. Global scope still rewrites from the live CONFIRMED set.

entries.title: gitRepos is an access list; only a single URL-shaped entry is a usable origin
entries.summary: agent.gitRepos is declared optional string[] and usually holds bare "Owner/Repo" access identifiers, not clone URLs. knownRepoRemoteUrl (in src/services/member-remote-url.ts, re-exported from execute-prompt.ts) returns a URL only when gitRepos has EXACTLY one entry AND it is URL-shaped (contains "://" or starts with "git@"); anything else yields undefined rather than a guessed URL.

entries.title: Sandbox supervisor shares the real ~/.apra-fleet/fleet.key with production
entries.summary: scripts/sandbox-deploy.mjs supervisors authenticate with the operator real ~/.apra-fleet/fleet.key when it exists (rooted at os.homedir(), not the sandbox root or APRA_FLEET_DATA_DIR); there is no sandbox-local fleet key.

entries.title: Streaks are anonymous bead arrays by the time they reach the doer dispatch, so the sync bracket carries no streak identity
entries.summary: groupStreaksFromLaneMetadata discards metadata.streak after grouping, selectStreaks never has a lane id, and the harvester has no streak -- so streak identity is unavailable on 2 of 3 pushCode:true paths, and there is no per-streak branch to key exclusivity on. Doer streak turns are serialized by globalDoerTurn in phases/develop.mjs.

entries.title: A role's member expression in role-policies.mjs is not role-unique, so it cannot identify a ladder
entries.summary: Three distinct roles share roleMember('planner') and two share roleMember('plan-reviewer'), so any guard that identifies a role's inline dispatch by its member routing expression alone flags other roles' ladders too.

entries.title: fleet.key is the member-JWT HMAC secret, so no console credential may be forwarded verbatim to a workflow package
entries.summary: getOrCreateKey() returns the HS256 signing secret used by jwt.ts sign and verify, so forwarding the raw fleet key upstream grants JWT minting; the console cookie and the /ext upstream credential are both derived digests, never the key.

entries.title: long_running task wrappers carry member.env only, never decrypted auth credentials
entries.summary: execute_command long_running writes env assignments into the persisted run.sh/run.ps1 with include {auth: false, member: true}, so decrypted credentials never land on the member disk; the synchronous path deliberately still carries auth env in its transient prefix.

entries.title: resolveServiceToken() has a read-only mode (createIfMissing: false) that passive probes must use
entries.summary: Passing createIfMissing: false to resolveServiceToken makes a token check truly read-only, returning null instead of minting a private/token file as a side effect of a mere probe.

entries.title: apra-fleet-client's createWorkflowEngine() is dead code -- workflow/ dir does not exist in that package
entries.summary: packages/apra-fleet-client/src/client/factory.mjs's createWorkflowEngine imports '../workflow/index.mjs' relative to itself, but apra-fleet-client's own src/ tree has no workflow/ directory in this repo state -- any caller must build the client manually (StdioTransport + McpClient + ApraFleet) instead.

entries.title: Slicing a runSprintCycle phase: pass reassigned locals both IN and OUT so the call site needs no conditional
entries.summary: Destructured parameters are assignable in JS, so a moved phase body can keep its `x = ...` statements byte-identical if the caller passes x in and destructures it back out -- which also makes the skip path a no-op without an `if`.

entries.title: The dispatchRole engine must spell agent( and ctx.withGitSync( literally or the guards lose it
entries.summary: dispatch-role.mjs destructures agent from ctx so the guards' call-site regexes still match its one dispatch, while the bracket and watchdog stay ctx-qualified and are asserted by regex instead.

entries.title: serve.mjs self-executes via isMainModule but exports no selfExecuting flag, so the workflow trampoline mis-handles it
entries.summary: serve.mjs runs serveMain() when argv[1] is itself, but exports no selfExecuting/main/run/default; runWorkflow() rewrites argv then reports did-not-execute, and calling serveMain() after rewriting argv starts two supervisors.

entries.title: makeTestLocalAgent defaults member os to the host platform, silently neutering OS-forcing test mocks
entries.summary: tests/test-helpers.ts makeTestLocalAgent sets os from process.platform, so a mock that forces a Windows-only branch is a no-op on a Windows runner and untested there.

entries.title: OS service manager is parameterized by ServiceId for two independent named services
entries.summary: src/services/service-manager/* uses a ServiceId-keyed descriptor table ('mcp-server', 'fleet-supervisor'), each with its own unit/plist/task name, restart policy and stop mechanism, so the two services can be registered, started, stopped or removed independently.

entries.title: exec-bd helpers resolve bd through the npm Windows shim; shell:true paths remain on Windows
entries.summary: Two drifted near-duplicate exec-bd helpers resolve bd on Windows via npm's generated bd.cmd shim; when no shim exists, execBdSync falls back to a shell:true invocation with no argument validation, and execBdAsync always uses shell:true behind assertSafeArgs.

entries.title: sandbox-deploy allocatePorts rejects adjacent port pairs, so fixed test fixtures must not use consecutive ports
entries.summary: allocatePorts() now rejects any candidate within abs-diff 1 of an already-chosen port (Math.abs(p - port) <= 1, which also subsumes the old exact-duplicate check), because the observed sandbox collision handed back a consecutive fleet/supervisor pair.

entries.title: An escaped backtick in any GUARDED_MODULES file trips the shell-command guard, even inside an Error message
entries.summary: shell-command-guard.mjs flags an ESCAPED backtick (a literal backtick inside a template literal) on any non-comment line of a guarded fleet-sprint module as backtick command substitution, even when it is prose in a thrown Error; unescaped backticks inside quoted strings are deliberately not flagged.

entries.title: A sprint's own reservation is always in GET /api/sprints while it deploys
entries.summary: The supervisor reservation ledger always contains the deploying sprint's own entry, so any 'non-empty sprints array => stop' deploy gate blocks every sprint from deploying its own work; identity must be compared exactly on sprintId.

entries.title: kb-reconcile-e2e fixture's import-source bible is also kb_export's target file
entries.summary: tests/knowledge/kb-reconcile-e2e.test.ts writes its merged branch-B import fixture to <repo>/.fleet/kb-canonical.json, the same path kbExport writes, so any change to kb_export merge semantics treats every fixture entry as already in the bible.

entries.title: Only roles with a kb-apply post-result step have their kb_captures recorded; the KB block no longer promises it to others
entries.summary: A dispatched role kb_captures output is applied only if its role-policies.mjs row lists kb-apply in postResult; planner, plan-reviewer, scoped-replan roles, deployer, integ-test-runner and regression-test-runner have none. The agent() wrapper now passes captureChannel=agentTypeAppliesKbCaptures(agentType) to kbKnowledgeBlock, so those roles are told to note findings in their own report instead of being promised the orchestrator records kb_captures; a persona shared across rows counts as no channel unless every row has kb-apply.

entries.title: openSyncBracketCount is a pure aggregate counter; cross-owner bracket overlap is legitimate except the opt-in code-write key
entries.summary: git-sync.mjs createSyncBrackets counts open brackets with no owner awareness; overlap across members is legitimate by default (D-push is serialized by the dolt push mutex). Only brackets passing exclusiveKey (CODE_WRITE_BRACKET_KEY, used by pushCode:true withGitSync) are tracked on a per-key stack and throw ConcurrentSyncBracketError on a crossing close. What keeps code-writing dispatches from overlapping is the globalDoerTurn FIFO gate in phases/develop.mjs; the exclusive key is a backstop for it being broken.

entries.title: execFileSync distinguishes a timeout from a non-zero exit by error.code, not error.status
entries.summary: A timed-out execFileSync sets code ETIMEDOUT, signal SIGTERM and status null, while a non-zero exit leaves code undefined and sets status to the exit code with stdout and stderr intact.

entries.title: VCS provider builders key the curl binary on os and the quoting dialect on shell
entries.summary: In fleet-sprint VCS provider builders, os selects the curl BINARY (curlBinary, OS-keyed) while shell selects the QUOTING DIALECT (shQuote, shell-keyed with an OS fallback); a windows+gitbash member correctly gets curl.exe with POSIX quoting.

entries.title: Extracting a fleet-sprint module out of runner.js breaks dispatch-safety-guard's EXPECTED_COMMAND_COUNT
entries.summary: test/dispatch-safety-guard.test.mjs hard-asserts the number of command()/agent() call sites in runner.js, so any move-only extraction that carries a command() call site out of runner.js fails that test even though every site stays compliant.

entries.title: Adding any duplicated top-level string to viewer state can turn plain /state fields into $ref markers
entries.summary: buildListStatePayload() dedupes every string of 24+ chars that occurs 2+ times anywhere in the payload, top-level fields included. Copying runId or timestamps into a new top-level object turns state.runId into {$ref:n} for consumers that read /state without resolveStringRefs.

entries.title: Supervisor reads fleet.key but never mints it; install and the server mint it
entries.summary: resolveServiceToken() uses <home>/.apra-fleet/fleet.key only if it already exists when the supervisor boots, else falls back to private/token for the process lifetime; fleet.key is minted by apra-fleet install and lazily by server-runtime code, not by apra-fleet start.

entries.title: guarded-modules-coverage's isAccountedFor() must compare full relative paths, not basenames, to avoid a nested-module collision
entries.summary: Per-guard violation-count baselines correctly compare by basename (guards report violations via path.basename), but the separate 'is every module registered at all' completeness sweep must compare full relative paths, because a nested file (e.g. phases/index.mjs) can share a bare filename with an unrelated top-level registered module (vcs-providers/index.mjs) and would otherwise be silently treated as already covered.

entries.title: Do not dynamically import every runner.js importer -- scripts/dolt-settle-integration.mjs runs main() at module scope
entries.summary: A test that imports each importer of fleet-sprint/runner.js to prove resolution will fire a live MCP connection and real dolt operations from that one file.

entries.title: install --force restarts a service it stopped, once the binary copy finishes
entries.summary: If the --force guard stopped a registered service, install restarts it after the binary copy (or lets the final service step re-register/start it), and always prints the restart command.

entries.title: Lockfile drift is invisible to npm test
entries.summary: A PR review that runs only 'npm test' cannot catch package.json/package-lock.json drift (e.g. a dependency override added to package.json without regenerating the lockfile), because npm test runs against whatever node_modules is already populated. Only 'npm ci' -- the reproducible-install path CI actually uses -- reproduces that failure.

entries.title: A blocks edge inside a streak lane splits the lane instead of sequencing it
entries.summary: groupStreaksFromLaneMetadata groups only the CURRENT ready set, so two co-laned beads joined by a blocks edge are never ready together and the lane degrades to one bead per round. streakOrder, not blocks, sequences work inside a lane.

entries.title: tests/setup.ts pre-loads src/paths.ts, so per-file data-dir overrides need vi.resetModules
entries.summary: Any test file that sets APRA_FLEET_DATA_DIR at module scope must call vi.resetModules() before dynamically importing FLEET_DIR consumers.

entries.title: wrapTool already accepts { text, structuredContent }, so adding a structured MCP response needs no tool-registry change
entries.summary: src/services/tool-registry.ts's wrapTool is typed to accept string | { text, structuredContent }, so converting an existing tool from a plain-string return to a structured one requires no edit at the registration site -- only the tool file and its direct consumers.

entries.title: sandbox-deploy.mjs getJson/postJson swallow 401 into null/false -- supervisor auth changes must thread a token through every out-of-package caller
entries.summary: getJson's `if (!res.ok) return null` and postJson's `return res.ok` make an unauthenticated 401 from the bearer-guarded supervisor indistinguishable from an unreachable server, so a supervisor-side auth change silently breaks scripts/sandbox-deploy.mjs's up/verify/teardown and its production-untouched check unless every call site sends the token.

entries.title: retry.infraResumeAttempts is a boolean gate, not a count -- a value above 1 is silently ignored
entries.summary: The engine reads infraResumeAttempts only as `> 0`; the resume loop bound comes from retry.resumeAttempts, and the loop re-iterates only on a repeated max_turns exhaustion, never on a repeated infra failure.

entries.title: The fleet-sprint goal-scope reopen guard was inert: 'P2' string compared against a numeric bead.priority
entries.summary: runner.js's goalMax is goalPriorityMax()'s STRING form ('P2') but the reopen guard compared it to a numeric bead.priority, so `3 > 'P2'` was a NaN comparison and the guard never skipped anything at any verdict site until normalizeGoalMax() was added.

entries.title: registerAllTools can be driven by a 4-line fake McpServer, unlocking every handler body for testing
entries.summary: The 'no test loads tool-registry.ts' gap is structural but trivially closable: a fake with tool()/server.sendLoggingMessage() records every registered handler and runs in ~2s.

entries.title: Mutate GUARDED_MODULES via a node --import preload to test guard registration without editing files
entries.summary: GUARDED_MODULES is a const binding but a mutable array, so a preload can append to it and exercise the guard tests against a larger registry with the working tree untouched.

entries.title: createSupervisor's auth guard is fail-open when no token is configured
entries.summary: server.mjs only enforces the bearer guard when deps.token or deps.dataDir was supplied; with neither, token stays null and requiresAuth/isAuthorized are never consulted, silently serving the whole /api surface unauthenticated.

entries.title: Node ESM circular imports between runner.js and its extracted fleet-sprint siblings are safe when confined to function bodies
entries.summary: Verified directly (a standalone a.mjs<->b.mjs repro, then live in prompts.mjs/worklists.mjs/abort.mjs) that a module split out of runner.js can import a still-runner.js-resident helper back, and vice versa, without any load-order failure, as long as neither side references the other's binding at top-level module-evaluation time.

entries.title: Workflow-package version gate must strip the v prefix and _hash suffix from serverVersion
entries.summary: serverVersion is not bare semver (e.g. v0.5.0_ab12cd in a dev checkout), and this repo has no semver dependency, so the range check is a hand-rolled fail-closed subset.

entries.title: tests/install-force.test.ts afterEach does not actually restore process.platform
entries.summary: Its afterEach redefines process.platform to its own current value, so a platform set by one test leaks into every following test in the file.

entries.title: The ASCII-only gate fails on shrink, so baselining generated files is a trap
entries.summary: check-ascii-only.mjs evaluate() fails on new-file, ratchet AND shrink findings; a baselined file that loses non-ASCII characters (or is deleted) turns npm test red until ascii-baseline.mjs is edited, and .beads/issues.jsonl is baselined even though bd regenerates it.

entries.title: The default VCS credential label's derivation is unfalsifiable by value, only by source shape
entries.summary: Re-hardcoding vcs-auth.mjs's DEFAULT_VCS_CREDENTIAL_LABEL to the literal 'github' left the whole test suite green, because DEFAULT_VCS_PROVIDER is itself 'github'; only a source-level assertion on the assignment (phase2-flagged-behaviour-gating.test.mjs) can gate it.

entries.title: degrade.classes, not degrade.kind, decides what a ladder fabricates -- and the integ runner's omission of 'infra' is the whole INCONCLUSIVE variance
entries.summary: The engine fabricates a value only for the ERROR_CLASSES a row lists in degrade.classes. The integ row lists schema and dispatch but deliberately NOT infra, which is what turns an envelope-less failure into an `inconclusive` record instead of a false passed:false.

entries.title: npm test cannot build packages/apra-fleet-ui-kit, so shell-ui tests fail on a clean clone
entries.summary: Root pretest runs only build:contract; apra-fleet-ui-kit is a tsc-built workspace whose dist/ nothing in the npm test chain produces, so shell-ui's vitest project fails import resolution on any clone that has not built ui-kit by hand.

entries.title: vitest injects __dirname, so typeof __dirname dual-path code takes the CJS branch in tests
entries.summary: Under vitest, modules like src/console/static.ts see a defined __dirname, so resolveDefaultShellDistDir() takes the CJS/SEA branch in-process; plain node -e (CJS eval) also defines __dirname/require globals. Only a real ES-module child exercises the ESM branch.

entries.title: originSlugFromUrl is a deliberately separate identity function from resolveProjectSlug's KB slugify -- do not merge them
entries.summary: member_git_status's origin-slug normaliser produces a human-readable host/path identity (e.g. github.com/apra-labs/apra-fleet) for grouping members by repo; resolveProjectSlug's slugify produces an unrelated, filesystem-safe KB scope key. They serve different consumers and are kept separate on purpose.

entries.title: The supervisor pins its own api-guard token at startup and never re-reads it
entries.summary: bin/serve.mjs resolves the credential guarding its own HTTP surface exactly once at boot, so a supervisor started before fleet.key exists rejects fleet-key bearers for its whole life.

entries.title: ClaudeProvider.detectUsageLimit treats a bare 429 as a usage limit without the limit-message
entries.summary: A 429 apiErrorStatus is classified as a usage limit on its own; the 'hit your <...> limit' message is only required for the non-429 terminalReason==='api_error' path.

entries.title: test/helpers/dispatch-pin-scanner.mjs has its own maskComments that does not model regex literals
entries.summary: The regex-literal desync fixed in fleet-sprint/dispatch-safety-guard.mjs still exists in the pin scanner's own maskComments, which drives the dispatch-pin and role-policy census tests; it is latent until a quote-bearing regex lands in a DISPATCH_LADDER_MODULES file.

entries.title: The client package carries a second hand-maintained copy of every tool field description
entries.summary: packages/apra-fleet-client/docs/api-reference.md has its own hand-written per-field glosses for tool parameters; nothing generates or tests it, so it drifts silently.

entries.title: pushBeadsAfter's real gap vs doltPushAfter was the non-throwing degrade contract, not retry/lease-renewal (those already lived inside doltPushAfter itself)
entries.summary: doltPushAfter() already contains retry (via runDoltStep's maxTransientRetries), mutex lease renewal, and settle-callback support regardless of caller; DoltSync.syncAfter()'s real value-add over a bare doltPushAfter() call is wrapping it in runDegradable(), which catches an unresolved failure and returns a structured {degraded:true} outcome instead of always throwing.

entries.title: apra-fleet-se's full real-bd test:integration suite takes ~4h; CI only ever runs one file in real mode
entries.summary: The full 'npm run test:integration' (scripts/run-tests.mjs real, no file arg) covers ~129 files against a real bd/dolt engagement and is documented as a once-per-sprint job, not a per-task/per-PR check; it also surfaces unrelated known carry-over regressions.

entries.title: ESM main-module guard must use pathToFileURL, not string interpolation, or it silently no-ops on win32
entries.summary: Comparing import.meta.url to a template-literal file:// string built from process.argv[1] is always false on Windows, so main() never runs -- no crash, just a silent exit 0.

entries.title: A sprint's own reservation is always in GET /api/sprints while it deploys
entries.summary: The supervisor reservation ledger always contains the deploying sprint's own entry, so any 'non-empty sprints array => stop' deploy gate blocks every sprint from deploying its own work; identity must be compared exactly on sprintId.

entries.title: Console cookie and per-package upstream credential use the same HMAC key but different labels, deliberately
entries.summary: Both the console's browser cookie and the /ext proxy's per-package upstream credential are HMAC-SHA256(fleetKey, label) with the SAME fleet key but DIFFERENT fixed labels, so one credential can never be replayed as the other.

entries.title: resolveProjectSlug prefers an explicit git remote URL over shelling git against repo_path
entries.summary: resolveProjectSlug(cwd, remoteUrl) slugifies remoteUrl directly when supplied and only falls back to `git remote get-url origin` against cwd, then the repo dirname, then 'default', when no URL is given -- letting remote members (whose repo_path is unreachable from the fleet server host) resolve to the same slug as a local clone.

entries.title: Measure a source-text guard's coverage by line-by-line injection, and count only the before/after delta
entries.summary: Injecting a real violating line at every line of every scanned module, then comparing the old and new checker, is what turns 'the guard scans clean' into evidence. Raw blind-line counts overstate the hole because an injection inside a comment or template text is legitimately not code -- only the delta, plus a classification of the residual, is defensible.

entries.title: Supervisor guard accepts the derived se credential on the bearer header only
entries.summary: isAuthorized falls back to comparing the bearer header against deriveUpstreamCredential(token, PACKAGE_ID), deliberately excluding the cookie path.

entries.title: dolt-sync.mjs sync.remote/tip memoization is process-lifetime, so multi-scenario tests must reset it between runs
entries.summary: fleet-sprint/dolt-sync.mjs memoizes each member's sync.remote answer and last-synced tip fingerprint in module-level maps for the whole process, so the first mock-sprint scenario in a process dispatches a real probe that later scenarios skip; comparing two runs in one process needs the reset triple between them.

entries.title: apra-fleet-se stale temp-home sweep uses an owner-pid liveness marker before its age gate
entries.summary: test/isolated-home-setup.mjs writes .owner-pid into each apra-fleet-se-test-run-* home. scripts/stale-temp-home-sweep.mjs never deletes a dir whose owner pid is alive, and applies the timeoutMs age gate only to dirs with a missing marker or a dead owner.

entries.title: fleet-se prerequisite summary is computed server-side and rides the fleet_status payload
entries.summary: The console Health page cannot probe fleet-se prerequisites itself; the summary rides the existing /api/fleet/status payload as an optional fleetSePrereqs string rather than a separate console route.

entries.title: SqliteProvider freshness verdicts must be suppressed, not re-hashed, when the repo anchor is unreachable
entries.summary: A repo_path that does not exist on this host (the remote-member case) must never fall back to process.cwd() as the freshness anchor, and must not be re-hashed against it either -- both checkFreshness and freshnessSweep now short-circuit to a no-op verdict via a shared anchorIsMissing() check instead.

entries.title: The sprint runner's dispatch inactivity budget is clamped to 1800s and no longer equals max_total_s
entries.summary: dispatch_timeout_s is applied as max_total_s unchanged, but timeout_s is passed through a min(1800, total) clamp, so the two budgets diverge at every default-args run and code or comments assuming they are equal are wrong.

entries.title: Provider-conditional body markers must be on their own line and cannot be quoted inside a fence
entries.summary: CONDITIONAL_MARKER_RE eats surrounding whitespace without requiring an own-line marker, and the resolver has no fence awareness.

entries.title: tests/cli-verbs.test.ts automocks node:child_process, so src/cli probes that shell out report absent there
entries.summary: vi.mock('node:child_process') with no factory in tests/cli-verbs.test.ts stubs execFileSync to return undefined, so detectFleetSePrereqs deterministically reports node and npm as NOT INSTALLED in that file regardless of the host.

entries.title: fleetStatus sets fleetSePrereqs at two separate json call sites; an empty registry only exercises one
entries.summary: fleetStatus builds its json payload in two places (empty-registry early return and the normal members path), each with its own guarded fleetSePrereqs assignment, so a test that resets the registry to empty covers only the first.

entries.title: vcs_credential_exec has two token placeholders with opposite quoting contracts, and mixing them up surfaces as a false 401
entries.summary: The bare vcs_token placeholder is substituted already quoted; the vcs_token_inline placeholder gets interior-only escaping for use inside caller quotes. Picking the wrong one double-escapes or leaves the token unquoted.

entries.title: A fallback message sharing the assertion's alternate keyword makes a test vacuous
entries.summary: checkDoltRemoteAbsent's bd-unavailable fallback messages all contain the word "unavailable", so the old combined assertion /Dolt-level remotes|unavailable/ was satisfied on any machine without bd without ever reaching the parser under test. Merged main closes this by probing bd --version first and asserting the two cases separately. The reusable trap: never OR an assertion's success keyword with its own fallback keyword.

entries.title: kb_bible_commit and kb_export share one bible admission predicate
entries.summary: kb_bible_commit now admits a CONFIRMED id only if filterProjectBibleCandidates (bible-basis-filter.ts) passes it, the same rule kb_export scope=project uses; failures are skipped with reason basis_mismatch.

entries.title: In Git Bash, a background job's $! is an MSYS pid that never equals the process's own process.pid
entries.summary: Under MSYS/MinGW bash on Windows, $! returns the MSYS-internal pid while a spawned native Node process reports a different native Windows pid via process.pid, so any script that proves identity by comparing $! against a pid the process reports about itself can never match.

entries.title: Editing the toString-embedded dashboard live script has three hard constraints
entries.summary: The supervisor dashboard client script is shipped as inline text via .toString() on each helper, which imposes declaration-order and no-window constraints enforced by an existing guard test.

entries.title: Supervisor OS service boots via the installed binary's own subcommand, not a resolved node path
entries.summary: The fleet-supervisor OS service runs '<BIN_DIR>/apra-fleet supervisor' instead of '<node> <serve.mjs>'; the node-path-resolution helper it replaced is gone, so supervisor-registration code must not reintroduce a dependency on an external node executable.

entries.title: runSprintCycle now hosts zero inline phase bodies, and that is mechanically pinned rather than described
entries.summary: After the final slice, runner.js builds no phase() label at all; phase-sequence-order.test.mjs asserts a zero-match shape scan over runner.js with a >=12 count across phases/* as its non-vacuity control.

entries.title: The service token reaches a runner only through spawner env injection, never through argv or a file read
entries.summary: coordination.mjs's clients resolve the token as opts.token ?? process.env.FLEET_SE_SERVICE_TOKEN, and only spawner.mjs sets that env var, so a runner started outside the supervisor's spawner has no credential for the guarded coordination routes.

entries.title: Usage-limit pause budget resets per re-dispatch, not per role
entries.summary: The usage-limit controller's MAX_WAIT_S/MAX_REPROBES budget applies per onUsageLimit invocation, so a role's total pause time across repeated clear-then-refail cycles is not capped.

entries.title: Vitest toHaveBeenCalledWith matches argument arity, so short .not expectations pass vacuously
entries.summary: A .not.toHaveBeenCalledWith with fewer args than the real call can never fail, silently turning a mocked-command isolation assertion into a no-op.

entries.title: The sync-bracket guarantee is mechanically scanned by a fifth guard, not just a convention
entries.summary: A fifth guard (unbracketed-push-guard.mjs) scans every guarded module for bare sync primitives outside git-sync.mjs, superseding the earlier claim that nothing enforced the bracket rule.

entries.title: normalizeMsysPathForPlatform is the required seam before path.resolve on any env-sourced path
entries.summary: Node's path.resolve does not understand MSYS /c/... paths and on win32 prefixes them with the current drive, so any filesystem path arriving from a Git Bash environment variable must go through normalizeMsysPathForPlatform first.

entries.title: scaledTimeout treats an empty APRA_FLEET_TEST_CONCURRENCY exactly like unset: unscaled base budget
entries.summary: scaled-timeout.mjs parses the env var with Number() and returns the unscaled base whenever the result is not finite or <= 1; Number('') is 0, so an empty-string export silently disables contention scaling with no warning.

entries.title: Dolt mutex sprintId+pid does not identify one pusher: all D-pushes in a sprint process share both
entries.summary: doltPushAfter acquires the supervisor dolt mutex with (sprintId || member, {pid: process.pid}), so concurrent member D-pushes inside one sprint process present identical sprintId and pid; any mutex logic that treats {sprintId,pid} as one client identity breaks mutual exclusion.

entries.title: The slow-lane stalled-session bounds bind to DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_S, not the inactivity budget
entries.summary: Both the lower and upper wall-clock bounds in the stalled-session slow test resolve through the watchdog pin, which is the row's maxTotalS, so the test cannot discriminate the inactivity budget from the total budget.

entries.title: Console route tests must spread importOriginal when vi.mock-ing src/tools modules
entries.summary: src/console/routes/fleet.ts validates every request body against the TOOL's own exported zod schema, so a bare vi.mock factory that only stubs the handler replaces those schemas with undefined and turns every validation case into a TypeError.

entries.title: Parent-NOTES staleness collector misses closed children because its bd list --parent call omits closed issues
entries.summary: collectParentNotesStalenessNotes in parent-notes-staleness.mjs lists a bead's children with plain `bd list --parent <id> --json`, which excludes closed issues by default, so the 'most recently created child' calculation is blind to closed children -- causing false negatives and false positives.

entries.title: StdioTransport.stop() is synchronous -- awaiting it with .catch() throws a TypeError
entries.summary: apra-fleet-client's StdioTransport.stop() returns undefined, so the common teardown idiom `await stop().catch(() => {})` throws TypeError inside a finally block and skips the cleanup after it.

entries.title: wrapTool already accepts { text, structuredContent }, so adding a structured MCP response needs no tool-registry change
entries.summary: src/services/tool-registry.ts's wrapTool is typed to accept string | { text, structuredContent }, so converting an existing tool from a plain-string return to a structured one requires no edit at the registration site -- only the tool file and its direct consumers.

entries.title: A migrated role's ladderAnchor deliberately matches ZERO agent() sites, so the inline-ladder guard's zero must be falsified per role
entries.summary: Once a role is marked migrated the anchor assertion inverts: matching no call site is the expected state, which means checkModules()'s zero says nothing on its own and has to be proven falsifiable by seeding a ladder for every role migratedRoleNames() returns.

entries.title: scripts/run-integ-suites.mjs always runs the whole apra-fleet-se test directory; no per-file scoping
entries.summary: The real-bd integ harness computes pending files from readdirSync(test).sort() with no caller-supplied subset, so reaching one late-alphabet file can take a long time behind the mock-sprint-* long poles.

entries.title: The dolt-orphan-sweep owner filter lives only in the generated shell string, never in JS
entries.summary: buildSweepCommand embeds the port range, age and --data-dir owner filter into a PowerShell or ps|awk string; sweepOnce reports every ORPHAN line as killed with no JS-side re-check, so only tests that inspect or execute the generated command can catch a dropped owner argument.

entries.title: schema-validated-fake-api.mjs only guards MCP tool INPUT drift; a tool's OUTPUT field rename is invisible to it
entries.summary: The workflow package's fake API validates outgoing payloads against real zod input schemas, but its canned responses are hand-typed; output shapes need a source-anchored pin like schema-validated-fake-api-output-shape.test.mjs.

entries.title: DEGRADE_STEPS is separate from POST_RESULT_STEPS because the reviewer's round session must be dropped on failure and kept on success
entries.summary: role-policies.mjs has three step vocabularies, and the split is load-bearing rather than tidy: a step in the wrong list gets the per-round reviewer's session handling exactly backwards.

entries.title: git says (fetch first), not (non-fast-forward), when the diverging remote tip was never fetched
entries.summary: A rejected push reports (non-fast-forward) only once the remote tip has been fetched; before that it says (fetch first), so the diverged verdict for that commoner case rests on the [rejected], failed to push some refs and updates were rejected rules, not /non-fast-forward/.

entries.title: A nested node --test child silently no-ops unless NODE_TEST_CONTEXT is stripped from its env
entries.summary: node --test sets NODE_TEST_CONTEXT on its own process; a child spawned with it still present returns empty stdout and exit 0 without running anything, so any nested-suite gate must delete it and then assert a non-zero '# pass' count.

entries.title: A runner.js back-import is safe for hoisted function declarations but TDZ-unsafe for const values read at module-load time
entries.summary: member-sync.mjs and beads-children.mjs can back-import resolveSettleShell from runner.js because it is a hoisted function declaration called only at runtime, but kb.mjs cannot back-import runner.js ROLE_DOER because KB_SELF_INJECTING_ROLES builds a frozen Set from it at module-evaluation time.

entries.title: gen-sea-config.mjs's SEA asset keys must equal the manifest key for sections read via getAsset(), not the disk-relative path
entries.summary: Unlike the extracted-to-disk sections (workflowRuntime, agentSchemas, builtinWorkflows, ...), the ui/ section's SEA 'assets' entries are keyed by the ui/-prefixed manifest key (e.g. 'ui/index.html'), because src/console/static.ts's seaSource() calls getAsset(UI_ASSET_PREFIX + requestPath) directly at request time.

entries.title: Workflow-package registration must target the fleet server ORIGIN, not server.json url
entries.summary: server.json's url is the MCP endpoint ('<origin>/mcp'), so handing it to createRegistration() makes the supervisor POST to a path the server 404s -- a retryable status, so registration silently retries forever.

entries.title: bdListScoped gives fresh STATUS but never fresh SCOPE -- scope always comes from the cached snapshot
entries.summary: A filtered bdListScoped() call issues a real bd list, but intersects it with scopeIds derived from the possibly-stale allBeadsSnapshot, so a bead CREATED behind the command() seam stays invisible until the snapshot drops even on a 'fresh' read.

entries.title: The runner signal-path tests only run on POSIX, so Windows-only verification proves little
entries.summary: tests/run-all-tests-timeout.test.ts skips its nested-grandchild-reap and outer-SIGTERM suites on Windows; run npm test on Linux/macOS before trusting changes to runner signal/kill paths.

entries.title: toolErrorText survives a contentless isError envelope, so the kb_ rejected-logging paths cannot throw
entries.summary: A degenerate MCP result of exactly {isError:true} with no content array still produces a usable log line ('no error text returned') instead of throwing inside the non-fatal handler.

entries.title: Workflow-package manifest paths are re-validated on registry read, not just on write
entries.summary: parseWorkflowPackageManifest runs both in the register route and in readPackages, so a hand-edited registry file cannot surface a path the route would reject.

entries.title: The pushCode:true dispatch set is four sites (doer + harvester, each with its resume), not two
entries.summary: Exactly four dispatch policies carry pushCode:true (doer and its resume, harvester and its resume); every other role dispatch is read-side. The flag lives in role-policies.mjs (doer :835, harvester :1262, read by dispatch-role.mjs into withGitSync) and is pinned by dispatch-sync-bracket-coverage.test.mjs.

entries.title: Phase 5 consumer migration end state is fully landed and pinned
entries.summary: readMemberVcsCredentialToken and parseExpiresAtFromProvisionText are completely deleted from fleet-sprint/ (not merely deprecated); buildCredentialReadCommand is deliberately kept dead-in-production/live-in-tests with no deprecation marker; member-provisioning.mjs and coordination.mjs have zero prose-branching (includes/match/toLowerCase) control flow.

entries.title: .fleet/ mixes a tracked deliverable (kb-canonical.json) with per-round scratch (planner-output.json)
entries.summary: Before adding a .gitignore rule under .fleet/, check git ls-files first -- .fleet/kb-canonical.json is a tracked, checked-in KB export deliverable, so a blanket '.fleet/' ignore rule would silently shadow it exactly the way this repo's own sprint-logs/ note warns against for directory-level ignore rules.

entries.title: npm install -g exiting 0 does not mean the binary is runnable
entries.summary: The installer must re-probe bd after a successful npm global install, because npm's global bin dir is routinely off PATH under nvm/volta and on Windows.

entries.title: Console route modules inherit the auth guard via the derived API namespace
entries.summary: Adding a route module under an /api/<ns>/... path automatically brings it under requiresConsoleGuard, because API_NAMESPACES is derived from the registered route paths rather than hand-maintained.

entries.title: Naming a test file mock-sprint-* enrolls it in phase3's nested run and real-bd budget
entries.summary: phase3-dispatch-engine-completeness.test.mjs discovers test/mock-sprint-*.test.mjs by prefix at runtime, so the filename alone decides whether a file is re-run in a nested child and counted into the real-bd nested-suite budget.

entries.title: Sandbox module imports in fleet-sprint tests must use pathToFileURL().href, not a raw absolute path
entries.summary: A raw absolute path handed to dynamic import() fails on Windows (parsed as scheme 'c:') and also fails on POSIX whenever the tmpdir path contains a space or '#'.

entries.title: KB knowledge reaches a dispatch by one of three paths, and a resume dispatch of a self-injecting role gets none
entries.summary: The agent() wrapper injects the knowledge block only for an agentType outside KB_SELF_INJECTING_ROLES; doer/reviewer get it from their prompt builders; a dispatch with no agentType, and every resume prompt of a self-injecting role, receives no block at all.

entries.title: Golden-transcript mocks ignore bd close failures, which resurface as a misleading stall-abort
entries.summary: The doer and integ-test-runner handlers in both golden-transcript test files run `bd close` via runCmd and discard its err, so a failed close is invisible and reappears cycles later as a stall-abort blaming the verifier.

entries.title: Validate, do not merely POSIX-quote, request data bound for a member command
entries.summary: Request-supplied values interpolated into member-bound command strings must be screened at the edge and then quoted for the TARGET member's shell, because the centralized shell-escape helpers are POSIX-only and the member may run PowerShell.

entries.title: copyDirResolved only utf-8 rewrites allowlisted text extensions
entries.summary: apra-pm install.mjs copyDirResolved round-trips files through a utf-8 string only for RESOLVABLE_TEXT_EXTENSIONS (.md/.json/.txt); everything else is copyFileSync, because the string round-trip corrupts binary bytes.

entries.title: The repo's commit hook ASCII check silently no-ops on macOS because it uses grep -P
entries.summary: A git commit of N changed files prints N 'grep: invalid option -- P' lines on macOS BSD grep; the commit succeeds and the hook's non-ASCII check never actually runs.

entries.title: strategy.execCommand resolves on non-zero exit; it rejects only on timeout, spawn/connection error or abort
entries.summary: Both LocalStrategy and RemoteStrategy resolve {stdout, stderr, code} regardless of exit status. A tool that must treat a failing command as a normal answer branches on result.code; one that relies on a throw for failure detection will never see a non-zero exit.

entries.title: launchAuthWeb reports launched before listen actually succeeds
entries.summary: launchAuthWeb returns {kind: launched} synchronously while openUrl fires only from the listen callback; on listen error openUrl never fires, so promise-wrapping callers must bound the wait.

entries.title: bd list --parent excludes closed issues by default; use the documented --all flag to include them
entries.summary: bd list --parent <id> drops closed children unless called with --all. Any child-counting or floor-seeding logic over bd list --parent must pass --all explicitly or it undercounts / resets to zero once all children close.

entries.title: POST /api/fleet/credential-store-update answers 200 for a credential that does not exist
entries.summary: credential_store_update reports a missing credential as prose, and the console route discards the tool result and echoes the request input, so the UI sees fabricated success metadata instead of the not-found error.

entries.title: killPidTree bounded wait is only non-hanging because isPidAlive treats a zombie as not-alive
entries.summary: waitForPidGone blocks the main thread with Atomics.wait, so libuv cannot reap a killed direct child; it returns promptly only because isPidAlive reports ps stat Z as dead. The two behaviours are load-bearing on each other.

entries.title: unattended has different read and write value shapes across list_members and update_member
entries.summary: list_members/member_detail emit unattended as false | 'auto' | 'dangerous' (boolean-or-string), while update_member's schema is an enum of the STRINGS 'false' | 'auto' | 'dangerous'; the shell-ui models these as two distinct types.

entries.title: Never interpolate an absolute Windows path into a JS string literal in a test-generated inline script
entries.summary: os.tmpdir() paths on Windows use backslashes, which are consumed as escape sequences when embedded in a JS string literal inside a generated node -e script, silently corrupting the path so the script writes to the wrong location.

entries.title: fleet-integrator merge gate splits read-only status from the one mutating action per loop
entries.summary: The integration-branch merge gate keeps PR-decision computation in a pure, read-only, fixture-testable script and confines every mutating GitHub action (merge, repair prompt, report) to the agent loop that consumes its JSON output, one action per PR per iteration.

entries.title: createChildBeadWithAllocatedId has four distinct post-probe failure outcomes and never releases after a landed create
entries.summary: The create, confirm and parent-link steps have separate failure paths: only a pre-create fault releases the allocator reservation, and confirm and link faults each throw their own orphan-naming error.

entries.title: update_member must keep owner in its zod schema and refuse it explicitly -- omitting the key would silently drop it
entries.summary: updateMemberSchema declares owner and then rejects it when existing.reservedBy is set; leaving owner out of the schema would make zod strip the key and return a success message while discarding the caller's intent.

entries.title: Supervisor ledger setScopeFreshness before start() overwrites the on-disk ledger
entries.summary: createLedger's transact() persists the current in-memory document; before ledger.start() has loaded the file that document is empty, so any setScopeFreshness call before supervisor.start() would write an empty reservations map over the real ledger.

entries.title: toolErrorText survives a contentless isError envelope, so the kb_ rejected-logging paths cannot throw
entries.summary: A degenerate MCP result of exactly {isError:true} with no content array still produces a usable log line ('no error text returned') instead of throwing inside the non-fatal handler.

entries.title: A fleet-sprint sandbox copy under os.tmpdir needs a node_modules symlink, and rmSync will not follow it
entries.summary: Copying fleet-sprint/ outside the repo breaks bare-specifier resolution for @apralabs workspace packages, so the sandbox must symlink the hoisted node_modules back in; fs.rmSync recursive cleanup unlinks that symlink without recursing into the real directory.

entries.title: Extracting a fleet-sprint module out of runner.js breaks dispatch-safety-guard's EXPECTED_COMMAND_COUNT
entries.summary: test/dispatch-safety-guard.test.mjs hard-asserts the number of command()/agent() call sites in runner.js, so any move-only extraction that carries a command() call site out of runner.js fails that test even though every site stays compliant.

entries.title: sprintMutexId pins the member-reservation key, not the engine run-state runId
entries.summary: cli.mjs reserves members with sprintId: branchName always, while effectiveRunId (run-id or branchName) keys only run-state files -- the two diverge under a supervisor launch.

entries.title: The /ext credential gate depends on the console cookie being SameSite=Strict
entries.summary: GET /ext/* stays unguarded and only withholds the derived upstream credential from unauthenticated callers, so the cross-origin protection rests entirely on the console cookie not being sent cross-site.

entries.title: Dirty-diff form baselines that move with a live prop need a per-field touched gate
entries.summary: A form that diffs current values against a baseline re-derived from a live-refreshing prop will flag untouched fields as dirty and silently revert concurrent changes; the console member drawer prevents this with explicit per-field touched flags.

entries.title: Viewer summary core fields refresh via broadcast(), so a new lifecycle handler must broadcast or call refreshSummary
entries.summary: state.summary core fields in createDashboardViewer are only kept current because refreshSummary() runs inside broadcast() plus the SIGINT/SIGTERM paths; a handler that mutates state without broadcasting leaves GET /state?summary=1 stale.

entries.title: launchd bootout unloads the job, so kickstart cannot restart it
entries.summary: On macOS, stopping a service with launchctl bootout removes it from the domain, so a later launchctl kickstart fails and the service stays down.

entries.title: reservedBy is the string mirror of Agent.reservation and member-reservation.ts is its only writer
entries.summary: Readers outside member-reservation.ts and list-members.ts still read the reservedBy string, so the two fields must always be written and cleared in the same updateAgent call; any site that clears one alone would make getReservation report a phantom holder.

entries.title: The child-id collision probe reads bd's error payload out of CommandError.details.text, and depends on structuredContent.exitCode
entries.summary: classifyBdShowProbeError can only tell a free id from a probe fault because FleetWorkflow.command() throws a CommandError carrying the raw output on details.text when the server reports a non-zero structuredContent.exitCode; on a server without exitCode no throw happens and every explicit-id child create fails closed.

entries.title: registerProjectRoutes keeps a narrow constructor and checks client methods per request
entries.summary: The /api/projects route module requires only client.executeCommand at construction; bind/overview endpoints check their extra client methods per request and answer 501 client-missing-method, so a partially capable client never breaks the CRUD surface.

entries.title: bdListScoped gives fresh STATUS but never fresh SCOPE -- scope always comes from the cached snapshot
entries.summary: A filtered bdListScoped() call issues a real bd list, but intersects it with scopeIds derived from the possibly-stale allBeadsSnapshot, so a bead CREATED behind the command() seam stays invisible until the snapshot drops even on a 'fresh' read.

entries.title: Console fleet routes return tool refusal strings as HTTP 200
entries.summary: Fleet tools that return a plain string surface refusals as HTTP 200 {text}, so UI callers cannot use fetch rejection to detect failure.

entries.title: memberIdentifier leaves both member_id and member_name optional, so zod alone cannot enforce 'a member is required'
entries.summary: src/utils/resolve-member.ts's shared memberIdentifier spread declares member_id and member_name as z.string().optional(), so every tool schema that spreads it accepts a body naming no member; the handler then returns a prose error string rather than failing validation.

entries.title: regression-test-playbook.md's Setup/Reset/Teardown headings appear as backticked prose mentions elsewhere in the file, so naive string.split('## Setup') is unsafe
entries.summary: Any script or test that wants to isolate the Setup/Reset/Teardown sections of regression-test-playbook.md by splitting on the heading text must anchor to a whole line (e.g. /^## Setup$/m), not do a plain substring split -- the file's own intro and cross-reference prose repeatedly mentions `## Setup`, `## Reset`, `## Teardown` inside backticks well before the real headings, and a plain .split('## Setup')[1] picks up that prose fragment instead of the actual section body.

entries.title: The usage-limit re-probe lives in its own module to keep runner.js dispatch-free
entries.summary: usage-limit-controller.mjs hosts the usage-limit wake re-probe (a real but deliberately unbracketed agent() dispatch) outside runner.js because runner.js's agent() census is pinned at zero now that every role ladder runs through dispatchRole.

entries.title: Exports-map subpaths must be proven from a sibling package
entries.summary: A package.json exports-map subpath is only genuinely verified by a bare-specifier import from another workspace package; relative imports inside the owning package's own tests cannot catch an exports-map typo or omission.

entries.title: parseVcsCurlOutput must take the status from the LAST line only
entries.summary: Taking the curl -w status trailer as the LAST line, rather than by any digit-matching search, keeps a response body's own digits-only lines from being mistaken for the HTTP status.

entries.title: retry.authSelfHealShortCircuits is inert at final-review's shipped attempts=2 and can only be observed by splicing attempts=3
entries.summary: The healed retry consumes attempt one, so at a two-attempt budget the short-circuit and the generic retry coincide; a mutation test must raise attempts on BOTH arms and vary only the flag, otherwise the field reads identically either way and looks unfalsifiable.

entries.title: A new role-policies budget name must be registered in the test harness in lockstep or the whole se suite throws
entries.summary: resolveBudget throws on an unregistered budget name, so renaming a budget in role-policies.mjs without updating the test fixtures turns a two-file change into ~130 failures across seven files.

entries.title: member-provisioning.mjs is barred from any includes/match/toLowerCase call
entries.summary: phase5-consumer-migration-end-state.test.mjs fails if member-provisioning.mjs contains any .includes( / .match( / .toLowerCase() call, even Array membership checks. Use Set, regex .test() or status checks instead.

entries.title: Console cookie on GET /ui is issued only to loopback socket peers, fail closed
entries.summary: handleConsoleRequest sets the apra_console_token cookie only when isLoopbackRemoteAddress(req.socket.remoteAddress) is true; a fake request with no socket gets no cookie, so tests needing the cookie must set socket.remoteAddress.

entries.title: Migrating a per-file callTool mock onto the shared vcs_credential_exec simulator silently replaces that file's own token literal
entries.summary: The shared mock vcs_credential_exec simulator substitutes two hard-coded tokens, so a migrated test that asserts on its own distinct token either goes red or, worse, keeps a no-leak assertion that can no longer fail.

entries.title: doltPullBefore records the remote tip before the caller re-lists, so a failed post-pull list is not retried
entries.summary: doltPullBefore records the new remote tip as soon as the pull succeeds. A caller that skips its re-list on remote-unchanged must also track whether its own last list succeeded; otherwise a list failure after a successful pull leaves stale data marked fresh.

entries.title: Vitest runs afterEach even when beforeEach throws
entries.summary: A fail-closed guard placed only in beforeEach still lets afterEach cleanup run against the unsafe state it was meant to block.

entries.title: code-intelligence telemetry USAGE_DIR ignores FLEET_DIR and APRA_FLEET_DATA_DIR
entries.summary: USAGE_DIR is hard-wired to homedir()/.apra-fleet/data/code-intelligence, so test data-dir isolation via APRA_FLEET_DATA_DIR does not cover usage.jsonl.

entries.title: The unref-ed exit-drain timer is never the last live handle -- the handle that outlives the window differs per path
entries.summary: strategy.ts and ssh.ts unref the exit-drain timer; it is safe because child stdio pipes (local) or the ssh2 TCP socket (ssh) stay ref-ed while draining matters. Every dispatch timer in these paths is unref-ed by convention.

entries.title: Member env-injection design: auth credentials must win name collisions with the plaintext env map
entries.summary: src/utils/env-prefix.ts merges a member's plaintext env map with its decrypted auth credentials, and deliberately lets auth values overwrite a same-named plaintext entry so update-rights-only callers cannot use the env map to blank or redirect a stored credential.

entries.title: The ctx.steps hook bodies are the one part of a migrated ladder no dispatch-pin test executes
entries.summary: dispatch-role-harness.mjs supplies recording stubs for ctx.steps, so runner.js's own step implementations are proved to be INVOKED but never proved to be CORRECT by the pin tests.

entries.title: Self-registering HTTP clients need a convergence loop, not a one-shot retry, when dependencies can appear in either order
entries.summary: The fleet-sprint supervisor's workflow-package registration re-resolves token, connection and origin on every pass of a capped-backoff loop instead of skipping once at startup, so a fresh install converges without a restart.

entries.title: Testing the exit-drain path needs a pipe-holder, not just a forced predicate -- otherwise the test is vacuous
entries.summary: The close handler and the exit-drain timer race to finalize(); a test only exercises the drain path if something withholds pipe EOF, e.g. a detached grandchild inheriting fd 1/2.

entries.title: SEA binary bundles workspace packages, so staleness inputs must include them
entries.summary: scripts/build-sea.mjs bundles src/index.ts with esbuild bundle:true and only cpu-features external, so imported workspace packages (fleet-api-contract, apra-fleet-client) are baked into the SEA binary and any freshness check must include their sources.

entries.title: A synchronously resolving sleep seam in an unterminating async loop starves the timer queue
entries.summary: Injecting a no-op async sleep into a retry loop that never terminates hot-spins on microtasks forever, so any setTimeout-based bound in the test never fires.

entries.title: Real bin/serve.mjs subprocess tests need concurrency-scaled budgets and a retried first probe on windows-latest
entries.summary: On the hosted windows-latest runner the first HTTP request to a freshly-listening bin/serve.mjs child can take well over 5 s under test concurrency (observed 9.6-11 s for supervisor-guard-e2e). Fixed per-request timeouts flake there; use scaledTimeout() with concurrency passed explicitly and retry the first loopback probe.

entries.title: Only scripts/run-tests.mjs makes scaledTimeout() non-inert in the apra-fleet-se suite
entries.summary: scaledTimeout() scales only when APRA_FLEET_TEST_CONCURRENCY is set, and scripts/run-tests.mjs is the single writer -- any raw node --test invocation silently runs every scaled budget unscaled.

entries.title: compose_permissions denylist patterns match a normalized form where only the FIRST colon becomes a space
entries.summary: normalizePermission() does replace(':', ' ') without a global flag, so host:port only collapses to 'host port' when no earlier colon appears in the payload -- a real evasion for space-bearing patterns.

entries.title: Source-text scanners that mask comments/strings must also recognise regex literals, via the shared canStartRegex/skipRegexLiteral
entries.summary: fleet-sprint guard scanners walk source over a comment-masked copy; a regex literal whose body contains a quote is misread as opening a string and desyncs the walk. The shared canStartRegex()/skipRegexLiteral() in dispatch-safety-guard.mjs must run before the string branch.

entries.title: Shared isolated-home test helper must run before any module that reads home eagerly, e.g. src/paths.ts's FLEET_DIR
entries.summary: applyIsolatedHome() (tests/helpers/isolated-home.mjs) sets HOME/USERPROFILE/HOMEDRIVE+HOMEPATH/APRA_FLEET_DATA_DIR/FLEET_SE_DATA_DIR and realpaths the temp home, but it is a no-op for any module already imported once, since src/paths.ts's FLEET_DIR is an eager top-level const.

entries.title: dolt-orphan-sweep owner scoping is opt-in via FLEET_SE_SWEEP_OWNER_DATA_DIR, and must stay opt-in
entries.summary: buildSweepCommand() accepts an owner data-dir prefix that both shell families enforce, wired by bin/serve.mjs from FLEET_SE_SWEEP_OWNER_DATA_DIR; it cannot be derived from FLEET_SE_DATA_DIR because the ephemeral --data-dir belongs to the member, not the supervisor.

entries.title: Supervisor summary pulls must be started before any per-row await in buildSprintViews
entries.summary: dashboard.mjs buildSprintViews only stays within one summary timeout because every row's pullSprintSummary promise is created up front, before the bulk bd fetch and per-row awaits; moving the pull inside the per-row body makes N hung children cost up to N timeouts.
